items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a compact connected oriented PL three-manifold with a finite simplicial triangulation having $t$ tetrahedra. Let $S$ be a compact properly embedded orientable normal surface for this triangulation, and let $b_2=\dim_{\mathbb F_2}H_2(M,\partial M;\mathbb F_2)$. If $S$ has more than $10t+b_2$ connected components, two distinct components cobound an embedded product $F\times[0,1]$ whose interior misses $S$ and whose vertical boundary lies in $\partial M$. Consequently a normal surface whose components are pairwise nonparallel has at most $10t+b_2$ components. The bound is for normal surfaces as supplied; it does not assert that an arbitrary incompressible surface has been normalized or that successive intersecting hierarchy cuts satisfy this same bound.

items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a compact connected orientable irreducible PL three-manifold, with a given finite triangulation. Here irreducible means that every locally flat PL sphere in the interior bounds a PL ball in the interior. Let $S$ be a finite union of disjoint compact connected, two-sided, properly embedded locally flat PL surfaces with given product collars and finite compatible triangulations. Suppose every inclusion of a component into $M$ is injective on fundamental groups, and every closed component has nontrivial fundamental group. Let $M\mathbin{\|}S$ denote cutting open along those collars, retaining two labeled faces for each component of $S$. Every connected cut piece is irreducible and its inclusion into $M$, after the collar identifications, is injective on fundamental groups. Both face inclusions of each cutting surface are injective into their incident pieces. The assertion applies at every finite stage of a hierarchy satisfying these hypotheses, regardless of genera, number of boundary components, or separating behavior. It does not assert existence or termination of a hierarchy, boundary-incompressibility, or superincompressibility.

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a compact connected oriented PL three-manifold with a given finite triangulation and nonempty boundary. Assume every interior locally flat PL sphere bounds an interior PL ball, and every properly embedded PL disk cobounds a PL ball with a disk in $\partial M$. Suppose every component $X$ of $\partial M$ has positive genus. For every integral class $\alpha\in H_2(M,\partial M;\mathbb Z)$ there is a compact properly embedded oriented locally flat PL surface representing it, possibly empty, with no sphere or disk components, no compressing disk, and no boundary-compressing disk. A compressing disk has interior disjoint from the surface and essential boundary loop on it; a boundary-compressing disk has boundary one essential proper arc on the surface and one arc on $\partial M$, and interior disjoint from both. Moreover, one can choose $\alpha$ and its representative $S$ so that
$$[\partial S\cap X]\ne0\quad\text{in }H_1(X;\mathbb Z)$$
for every boundary component $X$. Thus this representative meets every boundary component. No conclusion about absence of compressing annuli, pared superincompressibility, or existence of a whole hierarchy is asserted.

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a compact connected oriented PL three-manifold with a supplied finite simplicial triangulation containing $t$ tetrahedra. Assume every interior PL sphere bounds an interior PL ball, and every proper PL disk cobounds a PL ball with a disk in $\partial M$. Write $b_2=\dim_{\mathbb F_2}H_2(M,\partial M;\mathbb F_2)$ and $K=10t+b_2$. A finite disjoint family of compact orientable two-sided properly embedded locally flat PL surfaces, with product collars, no sphere or disk components, and no compressing or boundary-compressing disks, has at most $K$ components if its components are pairwise nonparallel. Here parallel means cobounding an embedded product with its vertical boundary in $\partial M$; no requirement on other components in that product is imposed.

Moreover, every given finite family of disjoint pairwise nonparallel connected closed incompressible orientable two-sided PL surfaces of positive genus extends to a finite family of maximum possible cardinality among such extensions. For that extension, every connected closed incompressible orientable two-sided PL surface of positive genus disjoint from the family is parallel in $M$ to some component of the family. This conclusion does not assert that a parallelism product avoids the other family components, or that any subsequent hierarchy terminates.

items.statement: Let $M$ be a compact connected oriented PL three-manifold with a fixed finite simplicial manifold triangulation $T$. Assume every interior PL sphere bounds an interior PL ball, and every proper PL disk cobounds a PL ball with a disk in $\partial M$. Let $S$ be a finite union of disjoint compact two-sided properly embedded locally flat PL surfaces, with product collars, no sphere or disk components, and no compressing or boundary-compressing disk. Then there is an ambient PL isotopy of $M$, preserving $\partial M$ setwise, taking the entire surface family to a normal surface for the original triangulation $T$. Boundary curves may move within $\partial M$; no fixed-boundary or prescribed-pared-pattern assertion is made. No smooth or arbitrary topological triangulation-existence result is assumed.

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a compact connected oriented PL three-manifold with nonempty boundary and a supplied finite simplicial manifold triangulation. Assume every locally flat PL sphere in its interior bounds a PL ball in its interior. Then there is a finite sequence of cuts along two-sided properly embedded locally flat PL disks whose boundary is essential on the boundary of the component being cut. Every cut piece remains irreducible and injects on fundamental groups into $M$. The terminal pieces are either parametrized PL balls or compact irreducible PL manifolds with nonempty boundary, every boundary component of positive genus, and every proper PL disk cobounding a PL ball with a disk in the boundary. All their boundary components inject on fundamental groups into their respective pieces.

If $X$ ranges over the original boundary components and $g(X)$ denotes their orientable genus, the number of cuts is at most $\sum_X\max(0,2g(X)-1)$. In particular, either some closed orientable two-sided locally flat PL surface of positive genus in the interior of $M$ injects on fundamental groups into $M$, or a finite disk sequence cuts $M$ entirely into PL balls. In the latter case reversing the cuts expresses $M$ as a finite union of parametrized balls with finitely many PL one-handles attached to paired boundary disks. This last description specifies the meaning of handlebody here; no smooth or arbitrary topological triangulation conversion is asserted.

items.statement: Let $M$ be a compact connected orientable PL three-manifold with a given finite compatible manifold triangulation. Let $S$ be a finite union of disjoint compact two-sided properly embedded locally flat PL surfaces, with given finite compatible triangulations and product collars. Then the inclusion of every connected component of $S$ into $M$ is injective on fundamental groups if and only if there is no embedded PL disk $D$ with $D\cap S=\partial D$ and with $\partial D$ not bounding a PL disk in the component of $S$ containing it. In the no-compressing-disk case, each boundary face of $M\mathbin{\|}S$ is injective into its incident cut piece, and every cut piece is injective into $M$. This assertion makes no irreducibility assumption and no smooth or topological triangulation-existence assertion.

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $N$ be a compact oriented irreducible PL three-manifold with a supplied finite triangulation. Let $P\subset\operatorname{int}N$ be an embedded collared PL product $F\times[0,1]$, where $F$ is a closed connected oriented finite PL surface of positive genus and each horizontal face injects on fundamental groups into $N$. Let $S\subset P$ be a compact connected orientable two-sided properly embedded locally flat PL surface, with product collar, no sphere or disk component, and no compressing or boundary-compressing disk in $P$. There is an ambient PL isotopy of $P$ preserving its boundary setwise that takes $S$ either to a horizontal slice $F\times\{s\}$, $0<s<1$, or to a vertical annulus $\gamma\times[0,1]$, where $\gamma\subset F$ is a non-nullhomotopic embedded PL circle.

In particular such a surface with nonempty boundary cannot have its whole boundary on just one horizontal face. Every connected closed orientable two-sided PL surface of positive genus contained in the interior of $P$ and injective on fundamental groups into $N$ is parallel in $N$ to each horizontal boundary face of $P$. The classification also applies simultaneously to a finite family satisfying the stated incompressibility hypotheses; its horizontal sheets have a consistent finite height order.

items.statement: Let $F$ be a compact connected oriented PL surface, possibly with boundary, with a given finite triangulation. Let $c\subset\operatorname{int}F$ be an embedded polygonal circle and suppose a compatible finite subdivision contains $c$ as a subcomplex. If $c$ is nullhomotopic in $F$, it bounds an embedded PL disk region in $F$. That region is unique unless $F$ is a PL sphere, in which case its two complementary regions are PL disks. More generally, every boundary component of a compact connected oriented finite PL surface other than a disk generates an injective infinite cyclic subgroup of its fundamental group. No smooth structure or surface triangulation-existence theorem is assumed.

items.statement:
Let $C$ and $C'$ be finite disjoint unions of compact three-manifolds with corners. Specify finitely many paired compact boundary faces $(F_e^-,F_e^+)$ of $C$, pairing homeomorphisms $a_e:F_e^-\to F_e^+$, corresponding faces of $C'$ with pairings $a'_e$, and product collars of these faces. Distinct face interiors are disjoint; face boundaries may meet. The quotient spaces obtained by these pairings are denoted $M$ and $M'$. Assume these specified gluings are manifolds, equipped with the given face-gluing PL structures when the PL conclusion is used. Let $g:C\to C'$ be a homeomorphism carrying each specified face to its corresponding face, and write $g_e^\pm$ for its restrictions. Assume that on every positive target face the discrepancy
$$k_e=(a'_e g_e^-)(g_e^+a_e)^{-1}:F_e^{\prime+}\longrightarrow F_e^{\prime+}$$
is supplied with an isotopy $k_{e,t}$ from the identity to $k_e$, equal to the identity on one common neighborhood of that face's boundary for all $t$. Then $g$ can be changed by an isotopy of $C'$ supported in collars of positive-face interiors to a homeomorphism $\widetilde g$ satisfying
$$\widetilde g_e^+a_e=a'_e\widetilde g_e^-$$
for all $e$. It consequently descends to a homeomorphism $M\to M'$. The correction fixes all residual boundary faces pointwise, so any prescribed residual-boundary map of $g$ and every transported annulus, torus, square, or marked-subset label there are retained. If the given collar data, maps and isotopies are jointly PL, the correction and descended map are PL. With oriented pieces and orientation-preserving piece maps, the descended map preserves orientation. The construction also applies inductively to every finite collection of prescribed hierarchy gluings. It asserts neither existence of the face isotopies nor a homotopy-equivalence-to-homeomorphism theorem.

items.statement: Assume full AC, and let $M$ satisfy the hypotheses of the finite PL boundary-spanning surface lemma: it is compact, connected and oriented with a given finite triangulation, every interior PL sphere bounds an interior PL ball, every proper PL disk cobounds a ball with a disk in the boundary, and all boundary components have positive genus. A compressing annulus for a properly embedded surface $S$ is a locally flat embedded PL annulus $A$ with one boundary circle $\gamma$ on $S$, its other boundary circle on $\partial M$, interior disjoint from $S\cup\partial M$, injective map $\pi_1(A)\to\pi_1(M)$, and $\gamma$ not isotopic in $S$ to a component of $\partial S$. Every integral class in $H_2(M,\partial M;\mathbb Z)$ has an oriented properly embedded PL representative, possibly empty, with neither sphere nor disk components, no compressing disks, no boundary-compressing disks, and no compressing annuli. Such a surface is superincompressible in the stated sense. One may choose the class so that its representative meets every boundary component in a nonzero integral boundary homology class. This conclusion is existence of a single surface family, not finite hierarchy termination or a theorem about prescribed pared-boundary markings.

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a compact connected oriented PL three-manifold with a supplied finite simplicial manifold triangulation. Suppose every interior locally flat PL sphere bounds an interior PL ball, and every proper PL disk cobounds a PL ball with a disk in $\partial M$. If $\partial M\ne\varnothing$, suppose every boundary component has positive genus. If $\partial M=\varnothing$, suppose instead that $M$ contains a connected closed orientable two-sided locally flat PL surface of positive genus injective on fundamental groups. All surfaces below are supplied with the finite compatible PL triangulations and product collars obtained by subdivision and cutting.

Then $M$ has a finite hierarchy to a finite disjoint union of parametrized PL balls. Its first stage cuts along a finite disjoint pairwise nonparallel family $S_0$ of connected closed positive-genus incompressible orientable two-sided surfaces. Its second stage cuts every component of $M\mathbin{\|}S_0$ along a finite properly embedded orientable family $S_1$ which meets every boundary component in a homologically nonzero boundary class and has no sphere or disk components, no compressing or boundary-compressing disks, and no compressing annulus with an essential non-boundary-parallel loop on that family. The remaining finitely many cuts are along proper essential PL disks. Every intermediate piece is irreducible and injects on fundamental groups into $M$, and every cutting surface injects into its incident pieces.

For the triangulation of $M$ with $t$ tetrahedra one may take $|\pi_0(S_0)|\le10t+\dim_{\mathbb F_2}H_2(M,\partial M;\mathbb F_2)$. After the first two stages, write $C$ for the components and $X$ for their boundary surfaces. The number of subsequent disk cuts is at most $\sum_C\sum_{X\subset\partial C}\max(0,2g(X)-1)$. No assertion of superincompressibility for $S_0$, or of compatibility with a prescribed pared locus or boundary pattern, is made. This is an unpared hierarchy theorem in a given finite PL structure, with no smooth or arbitrary topological triangulation transport.
